hints: Notice both waves share the same speed $340\text{ m s}^{-1}$ but have different frequencies $250\text{ Hz}$ and $300\text{ Hz}$.
Recall $v = f\lambda$, so the lower frequency gives the longer wavelength - calculate each $\lambda = v/f$.
Subtract the smaller wavelength from the larger wavelength to find the difference in $\text{m}$.
walkthrough: Identify the given data: $v = 340\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $f_1 = 250\text{ Hz}$ and $f_2 = 300\text{ Hz}$.
Use the wave equation $v = f\lambda$, rearranged to $\lambda = v/f$.
Calculate the shorter wavelength: $\lambda_2 = 340/300 = 1.13\text{ m}$ to 3 significant figures.
Find the difference: $\Delta\lambda = 1.36 - 1.13 = 0.23\text{ m}$ approximately. This is option A.

options.A: Difference of $1.36\text{ m}$ and $1.13\text{ m}$ is about $0.23\text{ m}$.
options.B: About $1.1\text{ m}$ is the wavelength of the $300\text{ Hz}$ wave alone, not the difference.
options.C: About $1.4\text{ m}$ is the wavelength of the $250\text{ Hz}$ wave alone, not the difference.
options.D: Much too large and does not follow from $v = f\lambda$ with $340\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
